title: Weekly Reorder Rate by Customer Segment
prompt: An online grocery service wants to track weekly reorder rates across customer segments. Generate a report showing every combination of customer segment and week in January 2024, displaying the count of customers who placed repeat orders that week. The report must include ALL segments for ALL weeks even when no reorders occurred (show 0, not NULL). A reorder is defined as a customer placing at least two orders in the same week. The `customers` table contains segment assignments; the `orders` table logs each order with customer_id and order_date. Output columns must be: `segment`, `week_start`, `reorder_count`. Order the result by `segment` ASC, then `week_start` ASC.
schema_ddl: CREATE TABLE customers (customer_id INT PRIMARY KEY, segment VARCHAR(20) NOT NULL, signup_date DATE NOT NULL); CREATE TABLE orders (order_id INT PRIMARY KEY, customer_id INT NOT NULL, order_date DATE NOT NULL, basket_value DECIMAL(10,2) NOT NULL);

composite_moves: cross join segments with weeks to create all combinations
identify reorders by counting orders per customer per week
coalesce counts to 0 for missing combinations

hints: You need every combination of segment and week to appear in the output, even when no reorders happened.
Build a skeleton by cross joining the distinct segments with a series of week start dates, then left join the reorder counts to that skeleton.

Use generate_series to create January 2024 Mondays, cross join with distinct segments from customers, then left join a subquery that counts customers with 2+ orders per (segment, week), and COALESCE the count to 0.
answer_key: WITH week_skeleton AS (SELECT generate_series(DATE '2024-01-01', DATE '2024-01-29', INTERVAL '7 days')::date AS week_start), segment_list AS (SELECT DISTINCT segment FROM customers), skeleton AS (SELECT s.segment, w.week_start FROM segment_list s CROSS JOIN week_skeleton w), reorders AS (SELECT c.segment, DATE_TRUNC('week', o.order_date)::date AS week_start, COUNT(DISTINCT o.customer_id) AS reorder_count FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE o.order_date >= DATE '2024-01-01' AND o.order_date < DATE '2024-02-01' GROUP BY c.segment, DATE_TRUNC('week', o.order_date)::date, o.customer_id HAVING COUNT(o.order_id) >= 2) SELECT sk.segment, sk.week_start, COALESCE(SUM(r.reorder_count), 0)::TEXT AS reorder_count FROM skeleton sk LEFT JOIN reorders r ON sk.segment = r.segment AND sk.week_start = r.week_start GROUP BY sk.segment, sk.week_start ORDER BY sk.segment ASC, sk.week_start ASC;

_meta.scenario: an online grocery service tracking basket size and reorder rates
